subject: Post-call: Model fit & regression concerns / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Model fit, evals, and next steps

Hi Sam 
- great to meet earlier. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we're all aligned:

What we heard
- Primary goal: improve product QA assistant accuracy for assembly intent extraction and safety-check suggestions.
- Current concerns: latency targets ~300ms p95, and recent drop in accuracy on edge-case prompts.

Recommended short list (based on your latency/cost targets):
- rw-14B-v2 (balanced: accuracy-first, moderate latency)
- rw-7B-quant (lower latency/cost for high-throughput routes)

Attachments I'm sharing:
- benchmark_report_v2.pdf — our initial eval across your prompt set (high-level numbers and failure modes)
- prompt_set_acme.csv — the canonical prompt/test set we used for the bench (please add any missing edge cases)

Immediate next steps
1) Your team to run the prompt_set_acme.csv against your sandbox (or we can run with NDA data).
2) We'll start a 2-week pilot on rw-14B-v2 with split routing to rw-7B-quant for low-cost slices.
3) If any degradation is observed, we'll pin the model version and investigate diffs (timeline: 48h for initial triage).

Vivek (solutions) and Dev (platform) are cc'd to scope the pilot mechanics and any pin/rollback playbook.

Would love to schedule a 30-min sync later this week to lock the pilot window — are you available Thursday morning PT?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-1212

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmerobotics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Model fit, evals, and next steps

Thanks Marissa, appreciate the clear recap. Quick update from our side after running a few tests this morning: we're seeing a noticeable regression in assembly-step extraction after the model update last weekend (we think the platform rolled to rw-14B-v2@20260530).

Examples attached (short anonymized transcripts) where the assistant either drops critical entity tags or hallucinates step numbers. I've attached three examples in the body here and will attach a small CSV of failing prompts.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood pin us to the previous snapshot/version while we triage?
- Can you share a diff of what changed between the two snapshots (we want to validate whether fine-tuning or tokenization changes are the likely culprit)?

We're happy to hop on a quick call with your SRE/eng to help reproduce.

Sam
Sam Taylor
Director of Product | Acme Robotics
sam.taylor@acmerobotics.com

Hi Sam, sorry to hear you're seeing regressions. Thanks for the examples, they help a lot.

Immediate plan (proposed):
1) We can pin traffic back to rw-14B-v2@20260528 (the snapshot prior to the 05/30 rollout) for your account while we triage. Pinning is a low-risk routing change and takes effect within minutes.
2) Dev — can you generate the binary/text diffs between 20260528 and 20260530 and share a short changelog? If there are tokenizer or training-data changes, we'll prioritize that.
3) We'll run the failing prompts from Sam against both snapshots and attach side-by-side outputs for your QA team.

Sam — if you approve the pin, we'll do it now and follow up with the triage artifacts. Also recommending a short blackout/maintenance window (15-30 mins) if we need to rollback fully.

Marissa, looping you to keep the account motion tight.

Thanks,
Vivek
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 02:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Model fit, evals, and next steps

Hey team — I ran a quick binary diff and attached model_diff_6.2_to_6.3.patch. Summary notes:
- No auth/serving changes observed; diff is concentrated in the final fine-tune step and a tokenizer update (subtle token merges).
- Likely root cause: tokenization merge changed how some domain-specific tokens (e.g. part IDs, "step-4") are chunked, which can alter attention alignment on short prompts.

Rollback/pin options:
A) Pin traffic for Acme to rw-14B-v2@20260528 (fast, immediate routing change; no restart) — recommended as first step.
B) Full rollback of default rollout to 20260528 across the region (requires 15-30 min maintenance window).

If you authorize option A I will:
- Create a pinned alias for your account and switch routing (ETA: <10 minutes).
- Run the failing prompt set against both snapshots and upload the side-by-side CSV to the Drive link in the thread.

Risks: pinning keeps your traffic on the older snapshot; if we find a specific tokenizer fix we can forward-port it to the newer snapshot and re-roll.

Please confirm permission to pin now.

Dev
Dev Patel
Platform Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.inference

Sam, thanks for the quick response and for sharing the failing examples. We will proceed with option A and pin your account to the 20260528 snapshot now.

Action items and timeline:
- NOW: Dev will pin rw-14B-v2@20260528 for Acme (ETA <10m).
- Next 24-48h: We'll run the failing prompt set side-by-side and share updated benchmark CSV + an annotated issue log (drive link shared).
- By 2026-06-04 EOD: Expect an initial regression triage report and recommended mitigation (tokenizer forward-port or targeted fine-tune).

Also confirming we'd still like to proceed with the planned pilot once we validate the outputs — we'll re-open the split routing to rw-7B-quant for lower-cost slices after the fix.
